rows.answer:
Whoever defames another shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both, or with community service under Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (which replaced Section 500 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860) [1][8].

Related provisions:
- Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 covers defamation, including its exceptions and punishments for printing, engraving, or selling defamatory matter [1].
- Section 222 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 covers prosecution for defamation, requiring a complaint by an aggrieved person or, in specific public servant cases, a complaint in writing by the Public Prosecutor before a Court of Session [5].
- Section 359 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 covers compounding of offences, specifying that defamation under Section 356(2) may be compounded by the person defamed [3].

Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 replaces sections 499 [7], 500 [8], 501 and 502 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

rows.question: When can a person accused of a non-bailable offence be released on bail?

rows.answer:
A person accused of a non-bailable offence may be released on bail when arrested or detained without warrant by an officer in charge of a police station, or when appearing or brought before a Court other than the High Court or Court of Session, except where there appear reasonable grounds for believing the person has been guilty of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, or is a cognizable offender previously convicted of specified serious offences [1]. This current provision under Section 480 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 has replaced Section 437 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 [1][7]. In such cases, as discussed in the Supreme Court judgment Gurcharan Singh & Ors. versus State (Delhi Administration), judicial discretion to grant bail is exercised subject to statutory bans and conditions, requiring reasons to be recorded in writing [1][11].
